method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis' (last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed), 45 claims; LICENCE: © The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne; Terms clause 5.2, personal use only; paraphrased and hash-anchored (read at https://www.rch.org.au/ (Terms and Conditions, clause 5.2)). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne 'RCH flowcharts for Anaphylaxis' (initial and refractory management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1), 16 claims; LICENCE: © The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne; Terms clause 5.2, personal use only; paraphrased and hash-anchored (read at https://www.rch.org.au/ (Terms and Conditions, clause 5.2)). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 rebuilds the hand-written Wave 1 page (which quoted RCH) as a paraphrase. All but one Wave 1 claim are carried over and re-anchored in the page as fetched on 2026-09-24 (see Unresolved). S2 anchors point into a text transcription of the two management flowcharts made in Wave 1; the flowcharts are images and were not re-read, so a person should re-check S2 doses against them before use.

claims.claim: **Definition (World Allergy Organization):** a severe hypersensitivity reaction affecting the whole body, which usually comes on quickly and can be fatal.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severe anaphylaxis** threatens the airway, breathing and/or circulation, and can happen with no typical skin signs and without shock.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **First steps:** take the allergen away if you can, and give adrenaline IM.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Possible anaphylaxis in a child with asthma:** adrenaline always goes first; asthma drugs come after.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Positioning matters:** lie the child flat, or sit them with legs out straight; they must not stand or walk until at least 1 hour after symptoms have gone.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **The diagnosis is clinical,** so emergency treatment follows the clinician's judgement, not a strict definition.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Breathing symptoms dominate in children** and can settle before treatment or before reaching hospital. Recognise them anyway, or the diagnosis will be missed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Abdominal pain and other gut symptoms** are not always anaphylaxis, but when they are severe consider it, so treatment is not delayed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Airway:** hard or noisy breathing · swelling of the tongue (lip swelling does not count) · throat tightness or swelling · a hoarse voice or altered cry · drooling in infants.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Breathing** (the commonest features in children): trouble talking · wheeze · a persistent cough, usually of sudden onset.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Circulation:** an infant who is pale and floppy · dizziness that persists · drowsiness coming on suddenly · collapse, with or without loss of consciousness · low blood pressure, fast or slow heart rate · cardiac arrest.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Gut symptoms depend on the trigger:** severe or persistent pain or vomiting counts as anaphylaxis whatever the cause; mild pain or vomiting counts after an insect sting or a parenteral drug, but not after a food.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Skin signs alone (hives everywhere, facial angioedema) are not anaphylaxis,** and 10-20% of cases have no skin signs at all.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Tests:** none for most children, since the diagnosis is clinical. Tryptase only in special circumstances (see below).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **WAO criteria:** anaphylaxis is highly likely when either one of two criteria is met.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **First criterion:** sudden illness (over minutes to several hours) involving skin, mucosa or both (e.g. widespread hives, itch or flushing, swollen lips, tongue or uvula), plus at least one of: breathing compromise (e.g. breathlessness, wheeze, stridor, lower peak flow, hypoxaemia) · low blood pressure or end-organ effects (e.g. collapse, syncope, incontinence) · severe gut symptoms (e.g. severe cramps, repeated vomiting), particularly after a non-food allergen.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Second criterion:** after exposure to an allergen known or very likely to affect that child, sudden hypotension, bronchospasm or laryngeal involvement (over minutes to several hours), even with no typical skin signs.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Timing depends on the trigger;** most reactions come on within minutes. Injected allergens (IV or IM drugs, stings) often cause symptoms in 5-15 minutes; foods typically by 30 minutes; oral medicines more slowly, usually over 1-6 hours.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **IM adrenaline 1:1000, volume by age and weight:** under 1 year (under 7.5 kg): 0.1 mL (see the note on small volumes), no device available · 1-2 years (10 kg): 0.1 mL; device 150 microg for 7.5-20 kg (under 5 years).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Continued:** 2-4 years (15 kg): 0.15 mL · 4-5 years (20 kg): 0.2 mL · 5-10 years (30 kg): 0.3 mL; device 300 microg above 20 kg (5 years and over).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Continued:** 10-12 years (40 kg): 0.4 mL · over 12 years (over 50 kg): 0.5 mL; device 500 microg or 300 microg above 50 kg (over 12 years).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Volumes below 0.1 mL** are hard to draw up accurately and invite a 10x overdose, especially in the stress of treating anaphylaxis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Devices:** EpiPen Jr 150 microg (0.15 mg) for 7.5-20 kg (under 5 years) · EpiPen 300 microg (0.3 mg) above 20 kg (5 years and over) · Anapen 500 microg (0.5 mg) above 50 kg (over 12 years).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Refractory anaphylaxis:** breathing or circulatory symptoms still need treatment after 2 correctly given IM adrenaline doses.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Not responding to the infusion:** ask critical care or the transport service for expert advice. ⚠️ An IV adrenaline bolus is advised against, though it may be used peri-arrest (e.g. 1 microg/kg IV).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Infusion protocol:** use the local one. In a non-tertiary hospital, the RCH protocol can be used together with a senior clinician and the paediatric transport service.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Peripheral IV adrenaline infusion:** add 1 mL of adrenaline 1:1000 to a 1000 mL bag of sodium chloride 0.9%, giving about 1 microg/mL; start at 5 mL/kg/hr (about 0.1 microg/kg/min).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Running it:** a dedicated line, pump and anti-reflux valves where possible · titrate to response and side effects · do not run high rates for more than 2 hours (fluid overload) · continuous monitoring of all vital signs, a 12-lead ECG and conscious state.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **No subcutaneous adrenaline:** it is absorbed less reliably, and can be slower, than IM.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not give** antihistamines, corticosteroids or leukotriene antagonists for anaphylaxis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Serum tryptase** plays no part in acute treatment. Order it only when the diagnosis is genuinely in doubt (e.g. idiopathic reactions, coexisting anxiety), or after talking to a paediatric allergist in special situations (e.g. stings, diagnostic agents, reactions around surgery).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Look for:** upper airway obstruction (stridor, swelling in the mouth) · lower airway obstruction (wheeze, respiratory distress) · shock (dizziness, pallor, collapse, hypotension, severe or persistent vomiting and/or abdominal pain) · with or without skin changes (itchy rash, redness).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Anaphylaxis', initial and refractory management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Initial%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Refractory%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Remove the trigger;** stop any infusion that is running.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Anaphylaxis', initial and refractory management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Initial%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Refractory%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Position:** flat, and not standing or walking; sitting with legs out if breathing is difficult; on the side (recovery position) if vomiting.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Anaphylaxis', initial and refractory management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Initial%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Refractory%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Adrenaline IM into the outer mid-thigh:** 10 microg/kg, up to 500 microg.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Anaphylaxis', initial and refractory management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Initial%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Refractory%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **As 1:1000:** 0.01 mL/kg, at least 0.1 mL and at most 0.5 mL; or use an adrenaline device.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Anaphylaxis', initial and refractory management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Initial%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Refractory%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **When in doubt, give the adrenaline.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Anaphylaxis', initial and refractory management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Initial%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Refractory%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Then** oxygen, and monitoring of SpO2, blood pressure and ECG.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Anaphylaxis', initial and refractory management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Initial%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Refractory%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Response absent or inadequate:** repeat the IM adrenaline 5 minutes later.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Anaphylaxis', initial and refractory management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Initial%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Refractory%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No better after two IM doses = refractory anaphylaxis.** Call for critical care help (senior ED, ICU, anaesthetics, transport service) and get IV or IO access.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Anaphylaxis', initial and refractory management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Initial%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Refractory%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Refractory:** give an IV sodium chloride 0.9% bolus of 10-20 mL/kg and start an IV adrenaline infusion through its own line.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Anaphylaxis', initial and refractory management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Initial%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Refractory%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Infusion:** follow local protocol, or for example put 1 mL of adrenaline 1:1000 into 1000 mL sodium chloride 0.9% and start at 5 mL/kg/hr (about 0.1 microg/kg/min).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Anaphylaxis', initial and refractory management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Initial%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Refractory%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Keep giving IM adrenaline every 5 minutes** until the infusion is running.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Anaphylaxis', initial and refractory management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Initial%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Refractory%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Ask critical care or the transport service for advice early.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Anaphylaxis', initial and refractory management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Initial%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Refractory%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Airway:** stridor or partial obstruction → 5 mL of adrenaline 1:1000, nebulised. Complete obstruction → follow the RCH pages on acute upper airway obstruction, emergency airway management (intubation) and can't intubate, can't oxygenate.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Anaphylaxis', initial and refractory management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Initial%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Refractory%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Breathing:** wheeze → salbutamol by spacer or nebuliser (see the life-threatening asthma management); apnoea → oxygenate and ventilate by bag-valve-mask, endotracheal tube or supraglottic airway.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Anaphylaxis', initial and refractory management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Initial%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Refractory%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Circulation:** shock → the adrenaline infusion comes first, with further sodium chloride 0.9% IV boluses (10-20 mL/kg); cardiac arrest → BLS and ALS (see the cardiopulmonary arrest guideline).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Anaphylaxis', initial and refractory management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Initial%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/Refractory%20anaphylaxis%20management%20flowchart.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Observe every child for at least 4 hours** where deterioration can be managed: from the last adrenaline dose, or from symptom onset if none was given.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Keep overnight** after more than 2 adrenaline doses, an infusion, IV fluid resuscitation or circulatory involvement · with a past biphasic or more severe first reaction · poorly controlled asthma · living far from emergency services · presenting late in the evening · anaphylaxis to a monoclonal antibody.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Talk to the local paediatric and/or allergy-immunology team** for high risk of fatal anaphylaxis · more than 1 adrenaline dose · a first diagnosis · anaphylaxis to a monoclonal antibody.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Think about transfer** for more than 2 adrenaline doses (refractory anaphylaxis) · an adrenaline infusion · care beyond what the hospital can comfortably give.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Discharge** can be considered once the child is stable and has needed no adrenaline for at least 4 hours.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Before home:** record the suspected allergen in the notes so it can be avoided · an individual ASCIA action plan (red for anaphylaxis, dark green for medication allergy) · 2 adrenaline injectors (EpiPen, EpiPen Jr or Anapen) supplied or prescribed; if a pharmacy is shut (e.g. overnight), consider keeping the child until morning · training with a trainer device of the brand prescribed, including positioning (no standing or walking during a reaction).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Drug-induced anaphylaxis:** these children usually do not get an adrenaline injector.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Also:** consider a MedicAlert bracelet · refer promptly to a paediatrician or a paediatric allergy-immunology specialist · optimise asthma care (diagnosis, action plan, preventer) · consider reporting under local rules.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **PBS:** EpiPen, EpiPen Jr and Anapen are PBS-listed for every child with a history of anaphylaxis, on authority prescription; they can also be bought at full price without a script.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Fatal anaphylaxis is rare in Australia** (about 1 per million people), in children mainly from food. Arrest more than 4 hours after the exposure is rare.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Fatal risk factors:** delayed adrenaline or delayed emergency response · being upright · poorly controlled asthma · peanut, tree nut or seafood allergy · adolescence · existing heart or lung disease.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Past severity does not predict the next reaction.** Getting the diagnosis right and discharging safely are what reduce the risk afterwards.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Currency:** PIC endorsed; page last updated October 2025.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Sources it cites** include the ASCIA acute management guideline (2024) and the ANZCOR anaphylaxis guideline (2025), both accessed 17 October 2025.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Anaphylaxis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anaphylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-24
